participants.note: Concept ACK; suggested covering additional option edge cases and diagnosed CI test loop failure
Approach NACK; wants validation handled centrally by the args handler rather than with piecemeal special cases
Concept ACK for parsing improvements, but recommends against increasing use of DISALLOW_NEGATION

claims.text: Cover related configuration edge cases: -timeout above INT_MAX, -mempoolexpiry overflow from hours to seconds, negative -txconfirmtarget wrapping, and zero/negation handling for -limitclustersize and -bantime.
claims.quote:
A few closely related cases seem worth covering as well:
- `-timeout` values above `INT_MAX` are narrowed before the new positivity check (similar ones were already attempted here and closed).
- Very large `-mempoolexpiry` values can overflow when converted from hours to seconds.
- A negative `-txconfirmtarget` wraps into the wallet's unsigned target and can make fee estimation fall back to `-fallbackfee`.
- Negating an integer option is documented as setting it to `0`, so `-nolimitclustersize` and `-nobantime` are equivalent to the zero values this PR explicitly accepts.

claims.text: The new test loop binds a std::string reference to temporary strings, causing CI to fail.
claims.quote: CI seems to fail because the new test loop binds a `std::string` reference to temporary strings.

claims.text: Argument validation should be handled centrally by the args handler itself rather than through piecemeal, bug-prone special cases (Approach NACK).
claims.quote: I think I'm Approach NACK at yet another piecemeal approach to a solution for this. This should be solved by the args handler itself, not with many different bug prone special cases.

claims.text: DISALLOW_NEGATION is only a partial fix that allows invalid zero values to slip through if zero values cannot be accepted, because it only guards against them being set in one path.
claims.quote: If your option can't accept zero values, DISALLOW_NEGATION is only a partial fix and may allow zeroes to slip through because you are only guarding against them being set ib a single path. Better to check for valid values one place instead of multiple.

claims.text: DISALLOW_NEGATION creates inconsistent user experience where -option=0 and -nooption behave differently without clear reason.
claims.quote: It creates inconsistent UX where -option=0 and -nooption have different behaviors without a clear reason, when normal behavior is for them to behave the same.

claims.text: The PR substantially increases use of DISALLOW_NEGATION, a flag that was intended to be used rarely and eventually removed.
claims.quote: DISALLOW_NEGATION was intended to used rarely and eventually removed (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/22766#issuecomment-944924866) and this PR seems to increase usage by a lot.

support.reason: There are lots of AI findings about these potential misconfigurations, so it would be good to close off as many of them as possible in one go.
for parsing improvements here; other changes look very good
